p3enqzi.s: Lower East Side counter making Sonoran-style burritos with soft, chewy flour tortillas, and never any rice.

pkwo456.s: Tiny, cash-only Neapolitan pizza kitchen on West Houston Street by the MacDougal handball courts, now with an Upper West Side sibling.

pmi4f5l.s: East Village sushi spot with a paradoxical deal: a sub-$100 omakase that is also all you can eat.

plepaee.s: Wylie Dufresne's pizzeria with fun twists on pizza-parlor classics. The Flatiron location closed on July 2, 2026; the Domino Park location stays open.

p1dxbiji.s: Brooklyn location of Tonchin, the Tokyo ramen shop founded in 1992, known for tonkotsu broth and house-made noodles.

psanpys.s: Manhattan location of Tonchin, the Tokyo ramen shop founded in 1992, known for tonkotsu broth and house-made noodles.

pi1tg8r.s: Greenpoint sandwich shop from the Takumen team, building katsu sandos on soft, pillowy Japanese milk bread.

p1t3s126.s: NoMad location of Temakase, a hand-roll bar with a no-tipping policy.

p1ano75z.s: Upper West Side Thai restaurant on Amsterdam Avenue specializing in Bangkok street food, decorated like a street market. Order a few snacks to start.

p1wvzy7x.s: The Halal Guys, the Midtown food-cart institution famous for chicken and gyro over rice with white sauce, now with shops around the city.

poqg159.s: NoHo piano bar with red velvet chairs and cheetah-print carpet. Bring a date for a pricey cocktail and a piano cover of a hip-hop hit.

p1bejk89.s: Ralph Lauren's clubby, gold-trimmed restaurant next to his Fifth Avenue Polo flagship. Famously hard to book.

phs2s6h.s: Buzzy, candlelit Greenpoint restaurant, one of the neighborhood's hottest tables.

p184o0tj.s: Italian restaurant and bar on Ludlow Street with a whitewashed dining room and an affordable wine list.

pap165o.s: Budget-friendly omakase in Kips Bay for solid sushi at a low set price.

p1bygkz0.s: Old-school, cash-only udon shop on St. Marks Place (once called Udon West), as good as it is cheap and an NYU favorite.

p6sx5jp.s: Quiet, minimalist Williamsburg sushi spot where you sit on cushions and build your own omakase from a platter of fish.

p14cyqr0.s: West Village Japanese spot specializing in seasonal rice-bowl dons, plus maki rolls piled high with ikura.

p1w29tkm.s: Stephen Starr's California-inspired restaurant on Park Avenue South, opened in 2014 with interiors by Roman and Williams.

prwa3ev.s: Slice shop from Roberta's alum Anthony Falco, known for a tangy sourdough cheese slice.

p124qequ.s: New York branch of Utshob, a Bangladeshi restaurant known for regional dishes, which opened on 1st Avenue in the East Village in 2024.

pvpvt6i.s: Contemporary Italian restaurant on West 13th Street in the West Village, with bold flavors and modern twists.

p1swbyte.s: First US location of a Japanese seafood chain, a few blocks south of Grand Central. A good option for affordable sushi in Midtown.

p95u6pv.s: Chinatown counter with a 20-person line for takeout roast pork over rice. Absolutely worth the wait.

pnlf8b2.s: Mott Street basement institution since 1938 for old-fashioned Chinese-American food like chop suey and sweet-and-sour pork, and countless late-night stories.

p1lhf73t.s: Chinatown branch of Xi'an Famous Foods, the Flushing-born chain serving the food of Xi'an, including spicy cumin lamb noodles.

p1j66hhn.s: SoHo shop doing one thing well: 12 kinds of rice-stuffed sweet tofu pockets topped with Korean ingredients.

p1fzyt1c.s: Family-run Mexican deli and grocery on Avenue A, serving authentic Mexican food since 2000.

p1lkiue4.s: Vietnamese-American bakery in Chinatown with a line out the door for pandan pastries and egg custard espresso. Get there early.

p76q684.s: Plain little breakfast and lunch spot on East 7th Street with an exceptional egg sandwich.

p16mxksw.s: Artsy, monochrome Williamsburg cafe that its owners want to be a neighborhood hub.

p3cx37u.s: Greenwich Village cafe open since 1927, said to have introduced Americans to the cappuccino. A classic late-night coffee stop.

p17p7z62.s: Cesar Vega's Elizabeth Street coffee bar, which has built a cult following by using only Nicaraguan beans.

p11ivjxq.s: SoHo cafe on Crosby Street serving Greek-inspired coffee, popular with the social media crowd.

pgqkplm.s: Nolita home goods shop and bakery from the Gem Wine team, with an excellent smoked trout sandwich.

pvdawrq.s: French bakery by day and wine bar by night, from Gautier and Ashley Coiffard, who started it as a pop-up from their apartment.

p1norw5x.s: First NYC cafe from Denmark's La Cabra, on 2nd Avenue in the East Village, with excellent coffee and the city's best cardamom buns.

pei5zag.s: Another La Cabra location from the Danish coffee roaster, famous for its cardamom buns and coffee.

p1uv29ta.s: Hugh Jackman's Laughing Man coffee shop on Duane Street in Tribeca.

plf51lg.s: "Third-culture" bakery in Cooper Square making some of the city's best and most inventive pastries.

p1dsz8l2.s: Homey East Village shop from Mary O'Halloran with crunchy, fluffy Irish soda bread and scones.
